Hi Ben,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We shared the draft Order Form with our legal and procurement teams and they flagged two items they want clarified before procurement can push the PO through:

1) Output ownership — the draft currently states Quantify.ai has ownership of the outputs generated by our use. Can you confirm Redwood's stance on customer ownership vs. service-level usage rights? Our preference is to retain title to outputs for internal productization.

Ben / team — drafted a concise set of redlines and an evidence checklist below. I kept the language narrow to address procurement's asks while protecting Redwood's ability to operate the service. Please review and tell me if any commercial tweaks are needed.

Proposed Order Form / MSA redline (to insert in Order Form under 'Use of Outputs' & MSA definitions):
- "Customer Outputs": "Outputs generated by the Service in response to Customer Inputs. Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive right to use, reproduce, modify and display Customer Outputs for its internal business purposes and to create downstream products for internal use or resale, provided that Customer shall not use Customer Outputs to train or improve any public Redwood models without a separate, written training license."

- Training / Feedback License carve (to MSA):
  - "Feedback/Training License": "Customer may provide Feedback or elect to grant Redwood a license to use Customer Outputs, usage telemetry and other non-personally identifiable service metrics for the purpose of model improvement only upon execution of a separate Training & Improvement Addendum. Absent such an addendum, Redwood will not use Customer Outputs to train models that are made available to third parties or in Redwood's public models."

Rationale and negotiation points for procurement:
- We can concede customer title and broad internal/productization rights (this removes a major procurement blocker).
- We require an explicit opt-in for training to protect model IP and avoid indiscriminate dataset ingestion.
- For customers who insist on training rights, offer a commercial addendum (revenue share / credits / fixed fee) and additional controls (data segregation, NDA, on-prem or Dedicated deployment).

Evidence checklist for procurement (one-pager items):
- SOC 2 Type II scope summary (link to report)
- Data retention policy + max telemetry retention for customer-specific logs (configurable per Account)
- Key management: KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed keys option
- Access controls: RBAC, audit logs, and request tracing per token
- Network/segregation: options for VPC / Dedicated pools / on-prem package
- Export & export-control statement and standard data processing addendum (DPA) link

Attachments to prepare: redlines_summary.pdf (two-page excerpt with clean and redline versions), evidence_checklist_onepager.pdf

Markus — FYI I inserted the phrase 'non-personally identifiable service metrics' to be precise. If you think we need narrower wording for telemetry, flag it.
